engines.note: The first engine: three.js r186 with RoundedBoxGeometry, Reflector, BufferGeometryUtils and SkeletonUtils; the box's second lock; recipes as scripts named by their BLAKE3 hash, built with their declared parameters, handed back as plain data (format 0) and a card (v1)
Each picture goes out once (box data format 1): textures name the picture they show in images, so a picture shared by many textures, as the kit's are, crosses once and is kept once

Controls: each control a built object offers (a tent's pitch, a pickup's doors and tailgate, a bag's open, a fire lit, a sealed asset's explode and build) is played in the box from 0 to 1 and leaves as numbers (box data format 2), with the object as built put back first; and each material with the kit's section caps says how its cut face looks (its colour, roughness and metalness)

Engine 4: what a viewer needs of a build as data (format 3: parts, labels, shells, cut, solver readings and moves, clips and poses), skinned actors with their skins, builds kept running in the box (live, tick, break, mend, end), rig catalogs on cards (their ids written as a card's); each control set back to its rest after its bake, so a mesh it reshapes leaves as built
